recommendation: Re-bin the per-site data at 40 bp per bin or less, the largest size that keeps the share below 5.0% at this heterozygosity: `--bin-size 40` for VCF and multihetsep input, or `fq2psmcfa -s 40` for a psmcfa file, which psmc-rs then reads with `--bin-size 40` so that the results are scaled with the same bin size.

message: This input records which bins are called (at least 10% of their 100 bases callable, fq2psmcfa's rule) but not how many of their bases are, as psmcfa does, so the fit treats every called bin as 100 bases, as C psmc does. 3.8% of bins are missing (N), and 191,470 called bins (1.0% of them) border those runs: they hold fewer than 100 callable bases unless a run starts or ends at a bin boundary. If missing data are also scattered in runs shorter than a bin, most called bins do, which this input cannot show. Partly callable bins show fewer heterozygous sites, which biases theta, the times and Ne low by about their missing share.
recommendation: To measure it, run `psmc-rs qc` on the data the psmcfa was made from: a VCF with its callable mask (--vcf-mask) or an all-sites VCF from `bcftools call -c`. It reports the share of callable bases of the called bins, and a fit of that VCF weighs each bin by its callable bases (--bin-callable auto), which removes the bias.
